article.title: The Regenerative Builder: The Mud, Sun & Slab Journal
article.description: Ishaan Bhargava's search for a genuinely sustainable home in Bengaluru — balancing embodied carbon, water neutrality, passive cooling, and startup founder bandwidth.
article.quote: "My house should compost, harvest, and breathe. Ideally before it impresses anyone."

learnings.text: Demand real performance utility bills over brochure green badges
Run total life-carbon including commute before choosing edge-of-city builds
Recognize founder bandwidth limits — buy focus now, phase the dream build to Plan 2031

moments.title: The bandwidth audit
moments.desc: Self-build required 11 hrs/week × 18 months. Ishaan's startup needed those same 18 months. Path A's premium was renamed 'the price of focus'.

tabs.name: Start Here
tabs.label: Start Here
checklistItems: Your environmental convictions are quantified, audited, and personally binding.
You ask for electricity bills before floor plans, and the communities that share them proudly are your tell.
You're torn between buying the rare proven thing and building the pure thing.
Your actual bandwidth — not your values — is the binding constraint, and admitting it took a while.
The peri-urban purity option quietly prices in an isolation you preach against.
You want the house to persuade people, and you suspect comfort persuades better than argument.
